subject.title: fix(secrets): resolve active exec refs locally

question: Should active, command-scoped, allowed exec SecretRefs permanently execute in the local command process before the gateway snapshot resolves all remaining paths?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, backward-compatible in resolved outcomes, and strongly proven, but it intentionally establishes a credential execution ownership boundary that requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Approve split per-path ownership
options.body: Execute only active allowed exec paths locally and retain gateway snapshot ownership for every remaining or locally failed path.

options.title: Keep gateway-first behavior
options.body: Preserve the current gateway-first fallback sequence and tolerate the recurring unavailable response until a different contract is designed.

options.title: Use the broader skip model
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96661, which skips gateway resolution for the command target set when an active exec ref exists, accepting weaker mixed-source ownership.

recommendation.title: Approve split per-path ownership
recommendation.body: Execute only active allowed exec paths locally and retain gateway snapshot ownership for every remaining or locally failed path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced both the central SecretRef resolver coverage and the affected reply-scoped resolution behavior.
